answer: Sybil resistance works by making every identity cost real money before it carries weight. Each agent locks a bond tied to verified work, and that bond stays at risk while it answers. One identity pays little, but a farm of clones must lock the same bond for every copy, so outlay grows linearly with headcount instead of staying flat. Honest miners lock once and reuse capacity; each fake key is a separate locked position. A swarm cannot reach meaningful quartz-level share without outspending the payoff, where the willow of marginal reward never covers the meadow of locked stake.
